evidence.observation: All four firms converge to 17 and maintain that price through round 25; consistent with coordination or independent convergence.
Price remains 17 after cost falls to 6, beginning an uninterrupted plateau through round 40.
Matches B at 17 throughout rounds 30–40 despite cost and demand changes; strongest sustained pairwise alignment.
Raises price to 19 while others hold 17, then returns to 17; weakens evidence of continuous four-firm coordination.
B and D simultaneously raise prices to 19 with unchanged cost and demand; one isolated matching move provides weak evidence.
B and D return to 18; no sustained coordinated increase or apparent punishment follows.
A and D simultaneously cut to 17, but demand falls and cost changes, limiting the inference of coordination.
All prices remain 18 despite lower cost; widespread price rigidity does not identify an agreement or a particular colluding pair.
B cuts 18 to 17 as D raises 12 to 13, with cost unchanged; simultaneous complementary adjustments suggest possible coordination.
D raises 13 to 14 while B cuts 17 to 16, again with unchanged cost; repeated paired adjustments strengthen suspicion.
C matches B at 16 several rounds after B's cut; delayed matching also fits independent competitive adaptation.
A remains at 12 throughout; its early matching with D lacks coordinated changes and provides weak evidence of agreement.
A and B raise prices after a cost increase; common cost exposure provides a legitimate explanation.
A and D retain price 20 after costs fall sharply, suggesting delayed pass-through, although B and C also retain substantial margins.
D prices below A, weakening evidence that their earlier matching prices reflect an agreement.
A and D charge 20 while B and C charge 19; repeated higher pricing merits scrutiny but does not establish coordination.
Matches A at 19 in every normal-demand round since round 14, establishing persistent pair-specific alignment.
A and D both maintain 19 after cost falls from 8 to 5; B cuts price.
Again matches A at 18 following their simultaneous reductions in round 25; matching persists in round 29.
Matches A during high demand, but demand-responsive pricing and recurring competitive price differences limit evidence of agreement.
A, C, and D charge 18 throughout all 40 rounds despite B repeatedly undercutting; persistent matching raises suspicion but cannot establish agreement.
B undercuts at 17 and earns more than each rival, demonstrating an observed incentive to depart from their common price.
B switches to 18 permanently while cost remains 8, ending its sustained undercutting without an accompanying cost change.
